1. HEAVY MENSTRUAL BLEEDING:

Focus on QOL rather than amount of blood loss

History:

-Nature of bleeding
-Related symptoms
⇨Pain
⇨IMB
⇨Pressure symptoms.
-QOL
-Comorbid factors
-Previous treatment.

Causes of HMB

Organic

Non-Organic

P Polyp

C Coagulation

A Adenomyosis

O Ovulation disorders

L Leiomyomas

I Iatrogenic

M Malignancy

N Not identified

Physical Examination:

1.In pts with Related symptoms
2. Mirena insertion.

Investigation: (lab Tests)

CBC – offered to all women (alongside treatment)

Coagulation Screen-(to rule out Willibrand disease VWD) , offered if

-HMB from menarche.
-Personal 0r family history of coagulation disorders.

Consider TFTS – if symptoms are suggestive.

•No role of serum ferritin and female hormone

Investigation of the cause:

→Offer pharmacological t/m before investigating cause of HMB if patient is low risk for
1.Fibroids
2. Adenomyosis
3.Histological Abnormality
4.Structural abnormality.

Investigation for cause of HMB:

1.Outpatient Hysteroscopy:

indications

•Persist IMB
•Persist Irregular bleeding
•Infrequent Heavy bleeding with OBESE / PCOD
•Taking tamoxifen
•Unsuccessful HMB treatment.

 

→Under L/A, (with or without oral Analgesia) in women

Who decline S/A, G/A or USG

→Endometrial Biopsy is taken @ the time of hysteroscopy
→Vaginoscopy is added as a standard diagnostic technique (3.5mm or smaller)
→Facility of see and treat.

2.Pelvic USG:

indications

•uterus is palpable abdominally
•Pelvic mass
•Obese post patient or where the examination is difficult or inconclusive.
•Larger fibroids

 

3.Trans Vaginal Scan (TVS):

indications

•Significant dysmenorrhea + Heavy menstrual bleeding (HMB).
•Bulky tender uterus, like Adenomyosis.
•Patient refuses or unsuitable then offer Trans abdominal scan (TAS) or MRI

MANAGEMENT

Mirena is 1st line in

1.No identified pathology

2.Fibroid <3cm

3.Adenomyosis

 

Not suitable/decline Mirena:

Non-hormonal

Hormonal

NSAIDS

COCP

Tranexamic acid

Cyclical oral progesterone

→Submucosal fibroids:

Hysteroscopic removal

→Fibroids 3cm or more:
•Refers to specialist care meanwhile offer tranexmic acid + NSAID
•Consider 2nd generation endometrial ablation.
•Consider UAE, Myomectomy or hysterectomy

Discuss limitations of each.

→Pharmacological treatment less effective for fibroids > 3cm

Pre – Treatment GnRH if fibroids are larger causes surgical difficulty or in women waiting menopause.

ENDOMETRIAL ABLATION:

⮤Generations:

1st: Operator dependent (hysteroscopic)

- Transcervical Resection of Endometrium.

- Roller ball Ablation

- Endo laser Ablation

2nd: Not Operator Dependent (Non-Hysteroscopic)

- thermal Balloon Ablation

- bipolar radiofrequency endometrial ablation

- Hydrothermal

Indications:

•patient Not fit or refuses for surgery
-Endometrium along with inner 5mm of myometrium need to be destroyed.

Contraindications:

1.Uterine size > 10wks.
2.Myometrial wall Thickness <8mm.
3.Structural uterine anomaly.
4.Histological uterine Anomaly.
5.Desire for future fertility

Endometrial Preparation:

Is done by

•Danazol
•GnRH Analogues
•Progestogen withdrawal
•Endometrial biopsy before ablation.

Contraception and ablation:

Sterilization with Essure along with ablation can be done

 

1st generations vs 2nd generation EA

Satisfaction rate, Acceptability, Operative time, Local anesthesia and Pre-post OP complications all are in favor of 2nd generation EA.

Peri – Operative Complications:

Metabolic Derangement.

→Transurethral resection syndrome
-In 1st generation due to glycine use leading to hyponatremia and hyperammonemia => MI, Coma, hemolysis, death

reference range of fluid deficit is 1.5 liter.

-Most Common in laser > TCRE> RBA
→Extra uterine thermal Visceral damage.

 

 

 

Long term complications:

1.Infection
1.Endometritis

2.Myometritis
3.PID

(Antibiotics after TCRE should be given)

2.Pregnancy related

miscarriage, PTB, ILUGR, ACRETA, RUPTURE, PPH, C/S

3.Post ablative syndrome

Worsening pain during periods

Synechiae formation

Compartmentalization

Hematometra

Un recognized Adenomyosis.

 

4.Post ablation tubal sterilization syndrome
•Occur when EA is combined with sterilization
•S/S: cyclical unilateral/ Bilateral pelvic pain with vaginal spotting.
•T/m: Removal of fallopian tubes + Hysterectomy.
